Resolves #18814

🌿 *A file that says "ship this" and a release step that deletes it were both correct in isolation. What this makes unsayable is that either one can be read alone — the header now owns its paths, so there is one statement per path instead of two resolved by luck of order.*

`buildScripts/release/prepare.mjs` rebuilt `.npmignore` as `header + verbatim .gitignore`. Every `!/dist/*` negation sat **below** the marker, in the replaced region, and the copy carries a bare `/dist` — so the **first release after those negations were added publishes an engine that cannot boot**. `dist/parse5.mjs` and `dist/marked.mjs` are imported at module scope.

Simulated against the tree, a release run deleted **12 rules**, with every check green beforehand, because `npm pack` reads today's file.

**Custom rules stay at the top of the file.** The copy is filtered instead: any rule for a path the header names is dropped from it.

Evidence: L2 (`npm pack --dry-run` against the real tree, plus the release composition run end-to-end) → L2 required. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | Outside-CI: a simulated release on this head loses **0** rules and packs every bundle. Red control: **12** lost on `dev`. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: `findRulesLostOnRelease`, built on the SHARED `composeNpmIgnore` the release step uses, wired into the CLI ahead of the pack. Twelve arms across `findRulesLostOnRelease` and `composeNpmIgnore — ownership is spelling-independent`, including one per `/dist` spelling. Fixture-driven, no hardcoded bundle list. |
| AC-3 | `/package.brain.json` and `/package-lock.brain.json` removed; both verified absent from the repo. No other header line names a missing path. |
| AC-4 | Outside-CI: `npm pack --dry-run --json` before and after — table below. |
| AC-5 | Filed as **#18823**, linked from #18814, with the premise corrected — `npx neo-app`'s `postinstall` installs the engine's devDependencies, so the scaffold CAN rebuild the bundles. |

## Deltas from ticket

**The ticket prescribed hoisting the negations into the header. That fails, silently — and the first version of this PR drew the wrong conclusion from the same measurement.**

| candidate | parse5 | marked | mermaid | highlight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| header, copy appended verbatim (the ticket's fix) | **MISSING** | **MISSING** | **MISSING** | **0** |
| custom rules last, copy appended verbatim (PR v1) | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | 2 |
| **header owning its paths, copy filtered (shipped)** | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | 2 |

Ignore files resolve last-match-wins, so a header negation loses to the copy that lands after it. I measured that correctly and then moved the *rules*, treating the generator as fixed. @tobiu rejected it on the rule that custom rules belong at the top, and he is right for a reason the measurement does not show: **ordering does not remove the contradiction, it only resolves it.** Both statements about `dist` stay in the file, correctness rests on position, and nothing in the file says so. It also splits the custom region in two and needs nine lines of comment to justify the second half — the accretion smell.

Filtering leaves **one statement per path**. The complexity was always there, previously as invisible order-dependence expressed as zero code.

**The filter is loud, because the trade would otherwise be even.** Every dropped line is logged with the header path that owns it:

```
Synced .npmignore with .gitignore (39 header lines kept)
  dropped from the copy: /dist  (the header owns /dist)
  dropped from the copy: /docs/output/*  (the header owns /docs/output)
  dropped from the copy: !/docs/output/class-hierarchy.json  (the header owns /docs/output)
  dropped from the copy: resources/content/sandman_handoff.md  (the header owns resources/content)
  dropped from the copy: resources/content/sandman_concept_slice.md  (the header owns resources/content)
  dropped from the copy: resources/content/computed-route.json  (the header owns resources/content)
```

All six are redundant against the header today. Swapping an invisible ordering rule for an invisible filtering rule would be no gain.

**AC-5 is left open on a changed premise, not skipped.** The ticket argued the bundles must ship because *"none can be produced on the consumer side"*. That is **false for the majority path**: `neomjs/create-app` generates a workspace whose `postinstall` is `cd node_modules/neo.mjs && npm i`, so the engine's own devDependencies land there and every bundle is buildable. It is only true for a direct `npm i neo.mjs`. That reopens the mermaid question — and a larger one — on evidence the ticket did not have, so it belongs in its own ticket rather than being answered here.

**One declared non-change, and its measurement is machine-dependent in one half.** The committed `.npmignore` is stale against `.gitignore`, so a release also syncs rules it predates. Measured on this head:

- **+26 files, all `apps/workstation/**`** — deterministic, and the half that matters for the decision: the workstation app would start shipping.
- **Removals vary by machine.** @neo-opus-grace measured **−8** harness hooks (`.claude/hooks` ×3, `.codex/hooks` ×2, `.kimi-code/hooks` ×3); I measure **−0** on mine. Neither is wrong: those are *generated-not-tracked* projections under ADR 0040 §2.7, so the removal count is whatever a given checkout happens to hold. This tree has no `.codex/hooks` at all and only the tracked `!.claude/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.mjs` exception. The engine-side rules land identically; what differs is which local files they can remove.

The sync working as designed, unrelated to this defect, and @tobiu's call. This PR leaves it, so a cut is not the first place anyone learns of it.

## Test Evidence

`npm pack --dry-run --json`, the only thing that decides what ships:

| tree | parse5 | marked | mermaid | highlight | total files |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` today | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | 2 | 5655 |
| this head | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | 2 | **5655** |
| this head, after the release composition | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | SHIPPED | 2 | 5681 |
| `dev`, after the release composition | *(12 rules deleted — all dist negations gone)* | | | | |

Byte-identical selection today: the repair changes durability, not contents. Composition is idempotent from its first run.

**Guard red control** — `findRulesLostOnRelease` against `dev`'s `.npmignore` names exactly what a release would drop: `/dist/*`, the five `!/dist/…` negations, `/dist/highlight/*` and its two files, `/docs/output`, and the two portal SEO files. Zero on this head.

**A rule the header owns counts as subsumed, not lost**, with its own arm. Otherwise every redundant `.gitignore` line under an owned path reports on every run with no available repair — which is what the first draft of the predicate did to `resources/content/sandman_handoff.md`.

`unit` spec: 26 passed.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] The monaco entries in `REQUIRED_ENTRIES` cannot be checked on a tree without `npm run bundle-monaco`; CI runs `bundle-browser-deps` first, so the job is the witness, not a local run.
- [ ] Next release: confirm `prepare.mjs` logs the dropped lines and their owners.

## Commits

- `19809ed158` — the defect, first shape (custom rules last)
- `5c7fcbd18c` — reshaped: header authoritative, copy filtered
- `8716b5e129` — RA-1/2/3: one shared composition, symmetric normalization, trigger inputs, message

## Evolution

Round 2 replaced the guard's foundations rather than patching them: @neo-opus-grace measured a false negative where `.gitignore` spelling `dist/` shipped 0 of 13 `dist` files with the guard silent, because the ownership test normalized one side and not the other. The composition now lives in one module imported by both the release step and the guard, so the guard can no longer certify its own restatement.

Opened with the npm-only rules moved *below* the `.gitignore` copy, which works by last-match-wins and needs no filter. Replaced after @tobiu's rejection: ordering leaves the contradiction in the file and hides the precedence, while owning the paths removes it. The measurement that killed the ticket's original prescription is unchanged; what changed is which component I treated as fixed.
